<!-- GENERATED by scripts/compile-contracts.mjs from contracts/rules. Edit the rule files, then run npm run contracts:compile. -->

- **invariant** `blocks/easing-offer-rule-over-motion-own`: `easingsForMotions(ids)` is the easing offer and it is a RULE over the motion's own tracks, never a table: `UNCLAMPED_PROPS` names the transform channels the renderer lets a value overshoot into, so an easing whose character IS overshoot or oscillation (`needs: 'displacement'` in `model/easings.ts` - back, bounce, elastic) is offered only on a motion that animates one of them. It takes EVERY phase the one easing setting will land on.
- **invariant** `blocks/universal-out-bank-any-data-block`: `motionPresets.ts` is the UNIVERSAL in and out bank for ANY data-block graphic - catalog, wizard import, agent-door scaffold, hand-made - authored directly as DATA with two keyframes per property, no emitter and no importer, and applied by the pure `applyMotionPreset`. It is NOT a category bank: `presetRegistry`'s banks are the catalog's tuned choreographies and need the structure contract they were written for, while a universal motion moves THE GRAPHIC AS ONE UNIT, which is what lets it promise to work everywhere.
- **trap** `blocks/clean-swap-inside-root-entrance-exit`: `applyMotionPreset` is a clean swap of the INSIDE-THE-ROOT entrance and exit only: it KEEPS `calls`, `dynamics`, `reveals`, `hides`, every layer whose element lives OUTSIDE the root, and every `loops` track on a property the motion does not write - the written track owns its property, so a loop there goes. It paces the step to the motion or to the kept content's reach, never shorter, and it CLEARS a styled lifecycle arrow, because a styled play or stop would play INSTEAD of the keyframes.
- **rule** `blocks/both-hosts-set-curve-both-read`: Both hosts SET the curve and both read it back FROM THE CODE: `easesForChoice(easingId)` is the `{easeIn, easeOut}` override handed to `applyMotionPreset` - 'auto' overrides nothing, so each motion keeps its tuned pair - and `currentMotionEasing` is its inverse, mapping the ease stamped on every phase's landing keyframes back to an `EasingId`, where all phases must agree and anything the list cannot name reads 'auto'. A motion that cannot SHOW the held curve drops it to Auto (`easingLegalForMotions`).
- **rule** `blocks/picker-draws-six-cards-ten-slide`: The picker draws SIX cards, not ten (`MOTION_FAMILIES`): Slide's four members and Wipe's two are one motion with a DIRECTION and render as arrows in the cell. The bank keeps all ten `MotionPresetId`s - every arrow picks a real one and a saved graphic names one.
- **rule** `blocks/reads-lit-card-back-data-times`: `currentMotionPreset(template, data, phase)` READS the lit card back from the data - times and values per target, ease ignored, because an easing is a modifier and not another motion. Nothing is stamped into the block for it, so a hand-edited timeline honestly lights nothing.
- **rule** `blocks/what-moves-root-direct-element-children`: `motionTargets` is WHAT MOVES: the root's direct element children that are DRAWN - hidden `.noacg-data-source` holders, script, style and form sources and inline-hidden elements are skipped - read off the HTML every time and each addressed by the most readable UNIQUE selector, an id, else a class no other element carries, else `root > :nth-child(n)`. The root itself never takes a track, because the interpreter owns its opacity.
